name: Cinematic taiko-style ensemble drums from white noise: velocity sets the amp and filter decay, a resonant 60 Hz high-pass plus low boost adds weight, a tanh soft clip and limiter go before a large-hall convolution reverb, with optional detuned sine, FM sub and round-robin sample layers
goal: Make big cinematic ensemble drums (taiko-like) with no recordings, using any synth with a noise oscillator, a filter, two envelopes and velocity sensitivity. Think in four categories: frequency, amplitude, time and timbre. Start with white noise; amp envelope with no sustain and a short decay, with velocity routed to decay (soft hits short, hard hits long and ringing) and a wide velocity-to-level range. Add a low-pass filter (about 1 kHz) with its own short envelope on cutoff, also scaled by velocity, so each hit starts bright and closes darker; add a little filter drive. EQ: resonant high-pass at about 60 Hz plus a low bell boost for weight, a mud cut, presence, a slight high shelf; add a little release so hits breathe. Soft clip (tanh waveshaper) driven a little by that low boost to mimic an overloaded ensemble, trim the output and the extreme sub. Put a limiter or maximizer, then a convolution reverb with a cathedral or large-hall impulse (shortened, low end tamed, highs damped, about 5 kHz lifted). Layers: several detuned sines with a pitch envelope for tone, an FM sub at 20-50 Hz, and a round-robin layer of rattly found-object hits with slight random pitch to avoid machine-gunning.

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Order matters: limiter before the convolution reverb, otherwise it crushes the tail.
The low boost into the soft clipper overdrives easily; a little drive goes a long way.
Values (1 kHz filter, 60 Hz high-pass, 20-50 Hz sub, about 5 kHz lift) are approximate from the transcript; tune by ear. The source used one particular synth; any synth with these modules works.

steps.action: Load white noise in a fresh patch; set the amp envelope to sustain 0 and a short decay; widen the velocity-to-level range.
steps.expect: Short percussive noise bursts with dynamic range.

steps.action: Route velocity to amp decay so soft hits are short and hard hits ring out long.
steps.expect: Quiet taps vs big booming hits.

steps.action: Add a low-pass (about 1 kHz) and a second envelope on cutoff with a short decay, opening bright at the attack and closing darker; scale its amount or decay by velocity and add a little filter drive.
steps.expect: A bright transient that falls into a dark body.

steps.action: EQ for weight: resonant high-pass at about 60 Hz plus a low bell boost; cut mud, add some presence and a slight high shelf; add a little amp release.
steps.expect: It reads as a drum, not filtered noise, with sub movement.

steps.action: Soft clip with a tanh waveshaper (small drive), trim the output, filter a little extreme sub.
Add a limiter, THEN a convolution reverb with a cathedral or large-hall impulse; shorten the decay, tame the low end, damp the highs and lift about 5 kHz.
steps.expect: A convincing big-room drum, with the tail intact.

steps.action: Optional layers: 3 detuned sines with a pitch-drop envelope (tone), an FM or sine sub at 20-50 Hz, and a round-robin layer of found-object or rattle hits with slight random pitch.

verification: Soft and hard hits differ clearly in length and brightness.
Repeated hits don't sound identical (round-robin or random pitch).
The reverb tail isn't squashed (limiter sits before the reverb).
